editorial:
Imagine the most awkward family vacation you can possibly think of, and then add a secret mistress into the mix. That is exactly what you get here. You follow Didier, a man who tries to leave his young lover, only for her to try and end it all. In a wild twist, he ends up being taken in by her family while she gets better. The vibe is a strange mix of funny and sad, making you wonder how on earth Didier is going to survive the social nightmare he created for himself. It is a messy look at love and guilt that feels like a chaotic dinner party where everyone is hiding something.

What really makes this work is the acting and the slow build of tension as the whole group heads on holiday together. You will feel the stress in every scene, but it is played for laughs most of the time. While the pacing is a bit slow in the middle, the payoff is worth it for anyone who loves character studies. If you want to see it, try renting it on Apple TV or hunting down a high-quality Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture. It is a great pick for a rainy afternoon when you want something different from the usual Hollywood stuff.
endingExplained: After the chaos of the vacation and the failed divorce attempt, Didier realizes he cannot simply escape his problems. The movie ends with him stuck in a loop of his own making. He finds that neither his wife nor his mistress provides the peace he wants. Instead of a happy ending, you see him trapped by his own indecision and the expectations of the people around him, leaving his life in a state of permanent, messy tension.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird family dynamics and dry humor.
